title: add kernel-hotspot tracer, kvcache offset histogram, and continuous batch pressure probe
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Motivation: It has been difficult to correlate kernel-level hotspots with KV cache layout and continuous-batching backpressure events in production traces. This PR introduces three complementary low-overhead probes and a small microbench harness to make cause-and-effect visible during perf investigations and automated regressions. Summary of changes: (1) kernel-hotspot-tracer: lightweight sampling probe that annotates scheduler and CUDA kernel entry/exit with a compact hotspot identifier derived from callsite and op-type. Emits NVTX ranges when available and falls back to short tracepoints for environments without NVTX. Includes FLOPS-adjusted counters to avoid over-weighting long-running kernels. (2) kvcache-offset-histogram: on-KVcache-access histogram recording offset distribution and small-window reuse counts to detect pathological stride patterns introduced by certain tokenizers or model layouts. Buckets are power-of-two with a dense region for accesses under 1KB. Exported as Prometheus-friendly counters and optional trace annotations for correlation. (3) continuous-batch-pressure-probe: emits an instantaneous batch_pressure gauge when the batch queue begins to back up and a sampled per-window pressure histogram for debug builds. Hooks into the batching controller earlier in the pipeline to capture producer-side pressure and includes a token-rate estimator to reduce noise from transient spikes. (4) simple_seq_bench microbench: executable to exercise variable-length sequences, stridey KV access patterns, and kernel-heavy ops; emits a compact trace and histogram CSV for offline analysis and dashboard ingestion. Design: probes are guarded by feature flags and sample rate knobs with defaults off in release builds. Histogram storage is ring-buffer backed and uses per-worker aggregators to minimize atomics. NVTX ranges are used when available with a fallback so traces are consistent across environments. Rollout: feature-gated behind telemetry.feature_flags.kernel_hotspot and telemetry.feature_flags.kvcache_hist, default disabled. Canary rollout plan: 5 percent traffic for one week then expand if metrics are stable. Tests: unit tests for histogram bucketing and ring buffer safety, stress test for multi-producer writes, and a short GPU integration job that runs the microbench in CI. Backwards compatibility: non-breaking and opt-in. Follow-ups: small observability ingestion parser update (observability-pack) and a future probe for kernel memory-bandwidth when cupi integration is feasible.

changes_summary: Introduce three low-overhead probes (kernel hotspot, KV cache offset histogram, batch pressure) and a microbench harness. Instrument batching controller and KV cache accessor; add unit and integration tests and docs for feature flags.

Lina Fernandez: NVTX ranges are helpful; please ensure the perf dashboard includes a concise legend mapping hotspot ids to callsites.
